title: A Second Day of Weekend Gains — and a Hard Lesson for the Short Book
lede: Crypto drifted higher again on Sunday, with Bitcoin up 1.75% and Ether up 2.3%. Behind the calm tape, the terminal's paper engine was finishing a painful audit of its short trades — and parking the whole lane.

paras: Bitcoin added 1.75% to close the weekend at $61,271, and Ether rose 2.30% to $1,724. Two green days repaired some of Friday's damage, but prices remained well below the week's opening levels.
Breadth stayed at 0% for a second straight day. The models' message was unchanged: this was a bounce inside a downtrend, not a turn.
Another 15 trades closed for −$231.36, again mostly shorts — SUI and HYPE shorts were stopped out and an XRP short was liquidated.

By the end of the day, the desk parked the short lane entirely. An audit of 25 closed trades showed the derived shorts had lost $495.85 at a 22% win rate, while longs were roughly flat. Shorts stay parked until the lane is backtested on its own; position sizing was also reset so a single stop-out risks about 1.5% of equity.
